description.narrative:
The project is an initial pilot of a longer three-year program called the Amasoja Youth Programme. It spans one year and three months—three months for the start-up phase and one year for implementation—with a focus on launching and validating the AYP Programme model.
The overall objective of the project is to empower youth aged 20–25 in Gugulethu through leadership training, personal development, and structured mentorship, enabling them to become role models and agents of change in their communities.
Expected results by the end of the 1.25 year project: •⁠ ⁠5 trained youth leaders engaged in ongoing mentorship and facilitation. •⁠ ⁠1 trained coordinator supporting programme delivery. •⁠ ⁠A tested curriculum and framework adapted to the local context. •⁠ ⁠Baseline data and evaluation systems established. •⁠ ⁠Stronger community engagement and institutional partnerships. •⁠ ⁠Increased self-confidence and civic engagement among participants.
The project will be implemented in Gugulethu, a township in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. The project will strengthen the capacity of youth groups in democratic leadership and advocacy. The project also establishes and reinforces connections between various societal actors and groups, including young people, family members, civil society organizations, schools, local leaders, and local businesses.

activity-date.narrative: The official start of the planning of the Amasoja Youth Leadership Programme according to SIDA Project Agreement 17712

recipient-country.narrative: 95% of the budget goes toward the Amasoja Youth Leadership Project in Gugulethu Township, Cape Town, South Africa.
